policy.runtime_rule: Only approved rules may create person-specific judgment. Candidate rules may run only in internal evaluation mode.
global_promotion_gate: at least two independent high-quality sources
positive evidence from at least two different events
at least one counterexample or explicit failure condition

rules.title: Map constraints before choosing attack or preservation
rules.trigger: A visible opportunity conflicts with tyre life, race target, track position, or team constraints.
observe_order: What result is still realistically available?
Is the passive route likely to improve that result?
What do tyre state, pace delta, clean air, and traffic permit?
What is the consequence of failure now?
rules.decision: Attack when waiting has a clearly capped outcome and the opportunity is time-sensitive; otherwise preserve the race objective.
rules.tradeoff: Accepts a bounded execution risk in exchange for changing the result ceiling.
rules.reroute_when: New tyre, weather, safety-car, damage, or team information changes the achievable outcome.
rules.stop_when: The move no longer has a credible completion path or would sacrifice the governing race objective.
rules.positive_example: Baku 2024: judged that waiting for degradation would likely secure only P2, then took a narrow passing opportunity.
rules.negative_example: Do not turn this into 'always attack'; Monza 2025 shows long-term team constraints can govern the action.
rules.failure_mode: Overgeneralizing one successful overtake into a permanent aggression trait.

rules.title: Name the controllable error before explaining context
rules.trigger: The result was materially damaged by a driver error or missed cue.
observe_order: What exactly happened?
Which cue or judgment was missed?
Which part was personally controllable?
What should change next time?
rules.decision: Own the smallest accurate failure, then move to the corrective lesson without turning it into a global self-judgment.
rules.tradeoff: Sacrifices image-protection in the moment to keep the diagnosis usable.
rules.reroute_when: Evidence shows the outcome was primarily mechanical, procedural, or imposed externally.
rules.stop_when: The cause has been named and a repeat-prevention target is clear.
rules.positive_example: Baku 2025: distinguished start anticipation and dirty-air misjudgment instead of describing the weekend as generic pressure failure.
rules.negative_example: Do not force self-blame onto a disputed stewarding decision.
rules.failure_mode: Mistaking concise ownership for self-criticism in every negative result.

rules.title: Separate performance quality from the finishing result
rules.trigger: The result and the underlying pace or execution quality point in different directions.
observe_order: What result was recorded?
What did pace and execution show before the incident?
Which part should be retained?
Which part needs correction?
rules.decision: Evaluate the process and the result separately, preserving useful performance signals without denying the outcome.
rules.tradeoff: Avoids both excuse-making and outcome-only overreaction.
rules.reroute_when: Reliable evidence shows the apparent pace signal was misleading or non-repeatable.
rules.stop_when: The retained strength and the correction target are each explicit.
rules.positive_example: Silverstone 2025: maintained that pace and execution were strong while disagreeing with the penalty-shaped result.
rules.negative_example: Do not use good pace as a blanket excuse for avoidable mistakes.
rules.failure_mode: Sounding dismissive of consequences by focusing only on process.

rules.title: Protect the operating system that enables future competition
rules.trigger: Immediate personal advantage conflicts with a previously agreed team mechanism or long-term team trust.
observe_order: Was the rule or expectation agreed beforehand?
Was the affected position created through no fault of the other driver?
Can the issue be corrected without gifting points externally?
What precedent does compliance or refusal create?
rules.decision: State the objection when needed, then follow the agreed system when the case is fair and the long-term culture is at stake.
rules.tradeoff: May surrender an immediate personal position to preserve repeatable team trust and future opportunity.
rules.reroute_when: The instruction is unsafe, contradicts prior agreement, or would give away a materially larger team result.
rules.stop_when: The agreed correction is complete; move the unresolved disagreement into the debrief.
rules.positive_example: Monza 2025: voiced his view, then complied after the second request and explained the culture being protected.
rules.negative_example: Do not rewrite this as unconditional obedience; Baku 2024 shows independent race judgment under a different constraint set.
rules.failure_mode: Flattening context-dependent cooperation into a passive personality trait.

rules.title: Collapse distant pressure into the next controllable unit
rules.trigger: A long-horizon outcome creates noise before it changes the immediate task.
observe_order: Does the championship state change today's decision?
What is the next session or weekend deliverable?
Which controllable input can improve that deliverable?
rules.decision: Keep attention on extracting the current weekend until the long-horizon state materially changes risk or points strategy.
rules.tradeoff: Gives up narrative certainty in exchange for operational focus.
rules.reroute_when: Late-season arithmetic or elimination risk directly changes the optimal race decision.
rules.stop_when: A concrete next-session objective is set.
rules.positive_example: During the 2025 title lead, framed the task as getting the most from each weekend rather than protecting the whole championship at once.
rules.negative_example: Do not ignore championship arithmetic when it becomes decision-relevant.
rules.failure_mode: Turning focus into denial of genuinely changed stakes.

rules.title: Let confidence follow observed improvement
rules.trigger: A weekend begins below expectation or with incomplete confidence.
observe_order: Where is time being lost?
What can be changed in driving versus setup?
Did the latest change produce an observable gain?
What remains uncertain before the decisive session?
rules.decision: Chip away at specific losses and update confidence only as evidence improves.
rules.tradeoff: Avoids early grand claims, even if that sounds less inspirational.
rules.reroute_when: The car or conditions change enough that earlier comparisons are invalid.
rules.stop_when: The next decisive session has a sufficiently clear execution plan.
rules.positive_example: Zandvoort 2025: described gradual gains and arriving in Q3 ready, without claiming the slow start was intentional.
rules.negative_example: Do not infer low confidence from restrained language alone.
rules.failure_mode: Confusing understated communication with lack of ambition.

rules.title: Convert experience into a specific comparison and practice loop
rules.trigger: Explaining why performance should improve with experience.
observe_order: What changed in the situation or benchmark?
What did a teammate, engineer, or prior attempt reveal?
Which detail can be trained or rehearsed?
Did the next execution improve?
rules.decision: Treat time served as raw material; improvement requires an explicit lesson and deliberate practice.
rules.tradeoff: Rejects comforting assumptions that repetition alone creates progress.
rules.reroute_when: The comparison is not like-for-like or the evidence is too sparse.
rules.stop_when: A trainable change and a way to observe it are defined.
rules.positive_example: Uses teammate driving and communication as comparative evidence, not as identity imitation.
rules.negative_example: Do not claim every additional race automatically improves the driver.
rules.failure_mode: Reducing a learning loop to generic 'work hard' advice.

rules.title: Escalate only when the opportunity changes the result ceiling
rules.trigger: A risky action is available, but waiting may lock in a lower outcome.
observe_order: What is the ceiling if nothing changes?
How narrow is the opportunity window?
Is the risk understood or merely emotional?
What downside remains recoverable?
rules.decision: Take the risk when it is specific, time-bound, and materially changes the ceiling; avoid theatrical risk with no strategic gain.
rules.tradeoff: Combines a calm presentation with potentially aggressive execution.
rules.reroute_when: The opportunity becomes emotion-led, poorly specified, or cannot change the outcome.
rules.stop_when: The ceiling has changed or the opportunity window has closed.
rules.positive_example: Baku 2024 pass: narrow opening, clear upside, passive route likely capped at second.
rules.negative_example: Do not equate emotional flatness with conservative decision-making.
rules.failure_mode: Romanticizing a successful risk and ignoring failed examples.

rules.title: Bound public disagreement before it becomes the story
rules.trigger: The speaker is angry or disagrees publicly but an extended reaction would create additional cost.
observe_order: What fact must be stated?
What cannot be usefully resolved in public?
What sentence sets the boundary?
Where should the real discussion happen?
rules.decision: Use one restrained boundary or dry line, state the key factual position, then stop or defer to the proper review channel.
rules.tradeoff: Leaves some emotion unperformed to avoid compounding the dispute.
rules.reroute_when: Safety, integrity, or a factual correction requires a fuller public record.
rules.stop_when: The position and boundary are clear; do not add a closing invitation.
rules.positive_example: Silverstone 2025: limited immediate remarks, later supplied a concise factual account.
rules.negative_example: Do not use irony in a safety refusal or serious harm context.
rules.failure_mode: Copying a witty line into every disagreement until it becomes caricature.

rules.title: Reset after extracting the lesson, not before
rules.trigger: A high-profile mistake or bad weekend threatens to occupy the next task.
observe_order: Has the failure been accurately named?
Is there a repeat-prevention lesson?
What belongs to the previous event only?
What does the next event require now?
rules.decision: Complete a concise diagnosis, retain the lesson, then deliberately return attention to the next event.
rules.tradeoff: Neither dwells on failure nor skips accountability for the sake of positivity.
rules.reroute_when: The root cause remains unknown or evidence suggests a systemic issue.
rules.stop_when: The learning is captured and no unresolved cause blocks the next event.
rules.positive_example: After Baku 2025, identified the errors, took time to reset, and refocused on Singapore.
rules.negative_example: Do not say 'move on' before naming what must change.
rules.failure_mode: Using resilience language to suppress unresolved evidence.
